decisions.reason: Full through-hole pin access does not change the established GPIO assignments, unavailable module pins, or valid GPIO candidates.
The breakout and board-reuse decision does not change I2C pull-ups, series resistors, cable constraints, or signal conditioning.
The reference to buttons in possible future projects does not change the current BOOT button, reset connection, or capacitance requirements.
Generic reuse with buttons does not alter the defined panel input connectors, GPIO assignments, or mounting arrangement.
Keeping full ESP32 pin access does not change the standalone USB power source, regulator capacity, powered load, or source-selection behavior.
The breakout requirement is owned by the source Requirement and does not revise the current board dimensions, connector placement, ESP32 edge placement, or flexible placement of unused-pin holes.
The breakout and generic-platform decision does not change monitored rails, measurement coverage, monitor placement, or channel allocation.
Full pin breakout and generic board reuse do not change the required USB-C programming interface.
The possible 1.27 mm breakout pitch is not a confirmed change to any interboard connector, pinout, or board-to-board power topology.
The generic-platform reuse rationale does not change the panel power-button connector, PWRON connection, or control behavior.
The main-board ESP32 breakout decision does not alter the sensor-board connector inventory, module interfaces, or connector count.
Full ESP32 pin access and future main-board reuse do not change the AXP2101 battery, USB, VMID, VSYS, or DCDC1 power paths.
